section_summary: This section comprises diplomatic correspondence, legal memoranda, telegrams, and administrative records from 1945 to 1948 concerning Japanese nationality laws and dual citizenship. It is centered around an extensive, annotated legal treatise by Thomas L. Blakemore detailing the acquisition, loss, and recovery of Japanese citizenship under Japanese statutes and regulations, with particular focus on American-born Nisei. The section also examines post-World War II citizenship status and repatriation policies for Formosans, British policy restricting renunciation of Japanese nationality by Anglo-Japanese dual citizens, and individual nationality investigations such as the property claim of Leo Ryotaro Ikeda.

subfiles.about: Japanese statutory texts and official gazette excerpts on citizenship transmitted as enclosures to a diplomatic despatch.
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains excerpts from Japanese official gazettes and statutory compilations setting forth citizenship and nationality laws and ordinances from 1899 onward. Transmitted as enclosures to a December 12, 1945 despatch from Tokyo, they provide the Japanese legal text confirming that no new nationality laws had been enacted since 1924.
subfiles.title: Japanese Legal Texts and Regulations Concerning Nationality (Enclosures to Despatch of December 12, 1945)

subfiles.about: A Department of State memorandum recording an inquiry from Alien Enemy Control regarding Japanese nationality laws and Tokyo's reply.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Records an Alien Enemy Control inquiry and Tokyo's confirmation that Japan enacted no new nationality laws since 1924.
subfiles.title: Department of State Memorandum Concerning Japanese Nationality Legislation Inquiries

subfiles.about: A Formosan resident in Washington petitions the Department of State for recognition as a Chinese national rather than a Japanese subject under the Cairo Declaration.
subfiles.from: Ai Chi Sai
subfiles.summary: Ai Chi Sai requests U.S. recognition as a Chinese Formosan citizen rather than Japanese subject pending passport issuance.
subfiles.title: Letter from Ai Chi Sai to Hugh Borton Regarding Chinese Formosan Status

subfiles.about: The Department of State replies to Ai Chi Sai regarding his request to alter his nationality status.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: The State Department regrets that it cannot take further action to change Ai Chi Sai's legal nationality status.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Ai Chi Sai Regarding Citizenship Status

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting translations and copies of Japanese Home Ministry Ordinance No. 9 and prescribed forms simplifying renunciation of Japanese nationality.
subfiles.from: Yokohama Branch, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.summary: This despatch transmits Thomas L. Blakemore's translation of Japanese Home Ministry Ordinance No. 9 of February 20, 1946, amending the Nationality Act Enforcement Regulations. The amendment enables persons residing abroad or in Japan to submit notifications of renunciation directly through the Minister of Foreign Affairs without official overseas representation. Enclosures include translated sample forms and original Japanese regulations.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 79 from Yokohama Transmitting Amendment of Japanese Nationality Act Enforcement Regulations

subfiles.about: A correction modifying a note concerning the age requirement for legal representatives submitting renunciation notifications under Despatch No. 79.
subfiles.from: Yokohama Branch, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.summary: Requests correction of Despatch No. 79 note 2 to specify that legal representatives present notifications when individuals are under fifteen.
subfiles.title: Correction in Despatch No. 79 Entitled Amendment of Japanese Nationality Enforcement Regulations

subfiles.about: The State Department instructs the Embassy in Nanking to ascertain whether Chinese authorities agree to SCAP's proposal to treat non-repatriating Formosans as Japanese nationals.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Instructs discreet inquiry whether China agrees to SCAP treating Formosans voluntarily remaining in Japan as Japanese nationals.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Telegram to American Embassy Nanking Regarding Status of Formosans in Japan

subfiles.about: The Embassy in Nanking reports that China will retroactively restore Chinese nationality to Taiwanese as of October 25, 1945, with provisions for expatriation.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Nanking
subfiles.summary: Reports Chinese regulations restoring nationality to Taiwanese retroactively to October 25, 1945, unless they declare intent not to regain it.
subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram No. 992 from Nanking Regarding Chinese Nationality Regulations for Taiwanese

subfiles.about: The State Department repeats Nanking's telegram No. 992 concerning Chinese nationality regulations for Taiwanese to the Political Adviser in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Transmits Nanking Telegram 992 to SCAP Tokyo regarding Chinese measures restoring nationality to Taiwanese.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Telegram to POLAD SCAP Repeating Nanking Telegram on Taiwanese Nationality

subfiles.about: A library and records charge-out slip recording the removal of telegram No. 992 from the central file.
subfiles.from: Department of State Division of Records Management
subfiles.summary: Records the charge-out of Nanking Telegram 992 from file 894.012/6-1746 on May 26, 1955.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge-out Slip for Nanking Telegram No. 992

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indexing Yokohama Despatch No. 136 regarding citizenship status of American-born Nisei regaining Japanese nationality through recovery.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Yokohama Despatch 136 transmitting a legal opinion on citizenship of American-born Japanese who recovered Japanese nationality.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note for Yokohama Despatch No. 136 on Nationality Recovery

subfiles.about: GHQ SCAP reports that determining the Japanese nationality of certain litigants requires information on their or their fathers' full legal domicile in Japan.
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser, GHQ SCAP, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports that determining Japanese nationality of certain litigants requires their or their fathers' full legal domicile in Japan.
subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram No. Z 20446 from SCAP Tokyo Regarding Litigants of Japanese Ancestry
subfiles.to: War Department and Department of State

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting Thomas L. Blakemore's extensive, annotated legal treatise on the acquisition, loss, and recovery of Japanese nationality under Japanese law.
subfiles.from: Yokohama Branch, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.summary: This despatch transmits a comprehensive legal memorandum prepared by Thomas L. Blakemore, revised with Meredith Weatherby, examining Japanese nationality legislation from 1899 through 1946. The study provides an exhaustive analysis of the acquisition of Japanese nationality by birth, marriage, acknowledgment, adoption, and naturalization, as well as provisions for loss and recovery of nationality, with particular reference to American-born Nisei. It details how statutory revisions in 1916 and 1924, together with the Family Registration Act, affected dual nationality, expatriation, and administrative procedures.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 253 from Yokohama Transmitting Memorandum on Acquisition, Loss and Recovery of Japanese Nationality

subfiles.about: A records charge slip noting that an enclosure to Tokyo Despatch No. 255 was charged out to RA.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Records that an enclosure to Despatch 255 from Tokyo was charged out to RA on October 8, 1947.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip for Despatch No. 255 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch reviewing British policy refusing protection or nationality certificates to Anglo-Japanese dual nationals renouncing Japanese citizenship, contrasting it with American practice.
subfiles.from: Yokohama Branch, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.summary: This despatch transmits correspondence between the Japanese Central Liaison Office and the United Kingdom Liaison Mission concerning petitions by Anglo-Japanese dual nationals to renounce Japanese nationality. British authorities refused to issue written certificates of British nationality, adhering to the principle that dual nationals are not entitled to British protection in their second country. Consul General Johnson contrasts this with American policy, which evaluates dual national cases individually and permits renunciation based on U.S. documentation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 488 from Yokohama Concerning Protection in Japan of Persons Possessing Japanese and Foreign Nationalities

subfiles.about: An internal memorandum summarizing background records on Leo Ryotaro Ikeda and noting his absence from the Japanese Family Register.
subfiles.from: Elisabeth B. Smith, Chief, Japanese Unit
subfiles.summary: Reports that Leo Ryotaro Ikeda's name was never entered in a Japanese Family Register and reviews his family file.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum Regarding Possible Japanese Citizenship of Ryotaro Leo Ikeda

subfiles.about: The Office of Alien Property requests a State Department legal opinion from Japan on whether claimant Leo Ryotaro Ikeda ever possessed or lost Japanese nationality.
subfiles.from: David L. Bazelon, Assistant Attorney General, Director, Office of Alien Property
subfiles.summary: David L. Bazelon requests an expert opinion on whether property claimant Leo Ryotaro Ikeda ever possessed or lost Japanese nationality.
subfiles.title: Letter from Office of Alien Property Requesting Legal Opinion on Leo Ryotaro Ikeda
subfiles.to: Richard W. Flournoy, Assistant Legal Adviser, Department of State

subfiles.about: The Department of State acknowledges receipt of the Office of Alien Property's request regarding Leo Ryotaro Ikeda.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: State Department letter acknowledging receipt of David L. Bazelon's inquiry concerning the nationality of Leo Ryotaro Ikeda.
subfiles.title: Letter to David L. Bazelon Acknowledging Inquiry Regarding Leo Ryotaro Ikeda
subfiles.to: David L. Bazelon, Director, Office of Alien Property

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits the Alien Property inquiry to Tokyo and requests an authoritative opinion on Leo Ryotaro Ikeda's nationality under Japanese law.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Transmits Alien Property inquiry and instructs the Political Adviser in Tokyo to obtain an opinion on Ikeda's nationality status.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 87 to POLAD Tokyo Requesting Legal Opinion on Leo Ryotaro Ikeda
subfiles.to: U.S. Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo

subfiles.about: The Political Adviser reports that Leo Ryotaro Ikeda lost Japanese nationality retroactively from birth and has always been legally considered an alien in Japan.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: William J. Sebald advises that Ikeda lost Japanese nationality retroactively from birth through failure to register and remains solely an American.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 355 from Tokyo Regarding Nationality of Leo Ryotaro Ikeda

subfiles.about: The Passport Division confirms issuance of a service passport to Leo Ryotaro Ikeda and the absence of any record of expatriation.
subfiles.from: Ruth B. Shipley, Chief, Passport Division
subfiles.summary: Ruth Shipley confirms the 1947 issuance of a service passport to Leo Ryotaro Ikeda and no loss of American citizenship.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum Regarding Passport Records of Leo Ryotaro Ikeda
subfiles.to: Joseph J. Keegan, Legal Adviser's Office
